small_guidance:
- The GEMM is M=128, N=16384, K=16384 — very tall-skinny in M. Add autotune configs with BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=128/256, BLOCK_K=32/64 (num_warps=8, num_stages=3-4) so a single program covers all rows, eliminating wasted M-tiles and improving L2 reuse on weight tiles. Also try BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=64 with BLOCK_K=128 to stress K-pipelining.
- Since M=128 fits in one tile, set GROUP_M=1 (or drop swizzle) — current GROUP_M=8 has no benefit when num_pid_m is 1-2 and just complicates index math.
- For softmax (N=16384), bump BLOCK_SIZE to 8192 or 16384 (single-pass persistent) with num_warps=16 and num_stages=2; the row fits comfortably and a one-pass online softmax with full-row residency removes the second load pass.
large_guidance:
- Fuse softmax into the GEMM epilogue per row: use a persistent kernel where each program owns a full row (BLOCK_M=1..16, BLOCK_N=N), streams K in chunks accumulating the full output row in registers/SRAM, then does online softmax + store in the same kernel. This avoids writing the 128×16384 logits to HBM and reading them back.
- Alternatively, split-K GEMM with atomic-free reduction across K-tiles into a per-row partial buffer, followed by a fused softmax that reads partials and reduces. With K=16384 and only 128 rows, the GEMM is bandwidth-bound on weight reads; a split-K (e.g. SPLIT_K=4-8) better saturates SMs.
- Store weight transposed once at init (Kn-major contiguous on K) so the inner `tl.dot` loads B with stride-1 along K; current layout has stride_wk=1 and stride_wn=K, which forces strided N access in the hot loop.
